page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no margin notes; catchword "pecora" at the right foot.

main_text.p: fet in uobis(deus)alienus:& uos teftes mei eftis,dicit Dominus, & ego Deus. Etiā antequā esset dies ego sum, & non est qui de manu mea eruere possit: ego operabor, & quis auertet (opus) illud? Sic dicit Dominus redemptor uefter,sanctus Israelis:Propter uos misi in Babylone,& deposui(potē tes) omnes ipsi fugitiui sunt unà cū Chaldeis,quorū clamor in nauib.(audiebatur.) Ego Dominus,sanctus uefter, creator Israel,& rex uefter.Sic dicit Dominus, q ponit in mari uiā,& in aquis impetuosis semitā.Ipse est qui educit currus & equos,exercitū & robur bellicū: simul iacebunt, & nō resurget: extinđi sunt(subitò,) sicut linum inquā extincti sunt. Ne recordemini prioru,neq; antiqua memineritis.Ecce ego facio nouū quid: iam confurget, & nunquid uos cognoscetis illud? pona enim uiam in deserto, & flumina in solitudine. Honorabit me bestia agri, dracones, & pulli struthionis: eo q, pofuerim aquā in deserto,& flumina in solitudine ad potandū populū meum,electum meum.Populus iste quem formauimihi,enarrabit laudem meam. Et tu Iacob non inuocasti me,cū tu Israel fatigareris propter me. Non adduxisti ad me pecora

page.notes: Printed "fet" at the line start is a word split from the previous page (likely "fet" = "sunt" or "set" as printed); left as printed. Chaldeis is printed with a ligature-like "d&" form, transcribed as Chaldeis. The parenthesised words "(deus)", "(opus)", "(potē tes)", "(subitò,)", "(audiebatur.)" are printed in parentheses and kept as such. "q," after "eo" is copied as printed.
